newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bank Rossiisky Kredit, others take KrAZ stake.
newsitem.headline: Bank Rossiisky Kredit, others take KrAZ stake.

text.p: Bank Rossiisky Kredit and a group of Russian and foreign investors have bought more than 47 percent of Krasnoyarsky Alyuminievy Zavod (KrAZ), one of the world's largest aluminium smelters, the bank said on Monday.
KrAZ is already a shareholder in Rossiisky Kredit, one of Russia's 10 biggest banks.

A spokesman for Rossiisky Kredit declined to say from whom the shares had been acquired, or how much had been paid for the shares in KrAZ, which like many aluminium companies has been subject to a bitter struggle for control.

Rossiisky Kredit said in a statement the acquisition was part of its policy of cooperating with enterprises in the ferrous and non-ferrous metals sectors, and the development of a financial-industrial group in these sectors. "Rossiisky Kredit's policy in the company will aim at creating and realising a programme to bring the enterprise out of crisis and restore the general situation to health," it said.
Its experience would enable it to carry out investment programmes worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
"This will help raise production at related metals companies, which in recent years have been in a difficult situation because of the dominance on the Russian market of foreign producers," it said.
The bank would defend the rights of strategic and portfolio investors in KrAZ regardless of the size of their holdings, it said.
